result.summary: This PR adds missing [[noreturn]] attributes throughout the codebase (sync.cpp, interfaces headers, libmultiprocess, test/fuzz code, RPC deprecation stubs, Qt exception handler) and turns on -Wmissing-noreturn (plus a related C++23 lambda-attribute warning) in the CMake build. It also switches a couple of bare exit() calls to std::exit(). The motivation, per the description, is that missing [[noreturn]] can cause compiler false positives and related issues, as surfaced during review of PR #35896.
result.problem: Compilers can emit false-positive warnings or miss real issues when noreturn functions aren't annotated; this affects contributors building with warnings-as-errors and can hide real bugs behind unrelated warning noise.

open_concerns: maflcko found a Clang bug/quirk where enabling -Wmissing-noreturn produces a spurious error for a function that does return in some builds, still under investigation.
maflcko reported (2026-08-31) that FuzzedSock/ZeroSock/etc. still fail to compile on Windows for both clang-cl and MSVC despite a workaround.
resolved_concerns: Style nits on line length and std::exit usage were addressed by additional commits.

result.card: This draft PR by fanquake adds missing [[noreturn]] attributes throughout the codebase (sync.cpp, interfaces headers, libmultiprocess, RPC/mining stubs, Qt exception handler, fuzz test harness) and enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning in CMake, aiming to catch a class of compiler false positives noted during review of PR #35896. The strongest evidence of value is that turning on the warning surfaced real cross-platform issues: a suspected Clang compiler bug and an unresolved Windows (clang-cl/MSVC) compile failure reported by maflcko on 2026-08-31. Review sentiment is positive with Concept ACKs from hebasto and stickies-v and no objections, but the author explicitly said (2026-08-18) the PR will stay in draft until the next libmultiprocess subtree update lands, and CI is currently failing. Companion fixes have been split out upstream into bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#339 and bitcoin-core/leveldb-subtree#64. Most of the individual file changes are cosmetic attribute additions with no behavioral impact; the main substantive value is in the build/CI warning-hygiene and the fuzz-harness fixes.
